annotations.description: DSV3 Analyst chose to take Beast Within with Thoughtseize from Qwen3L Dreamer's hand. While Beast Within is a versatile instant-speed removal spell that could threaten DSV3's permanents (including key enchantments like Pernicious Deed or Sylvan Library), Rishkar's Expertise is arguably the highest-impact card in the hand. Rishkar's Expertise can generate massive card advantage by drawing cards equal to greatest power AND casting a free spell with MV 5 or less. In a multiplayer game, denying that kind of card advantage engine is typically more impactful than removing a reactive removal spell. Rishkar, Peema Renegade is also notable as it enables mana ramp and enables Rishkar's Expertise to draw more cards. However, Beast Within is the card most likely to directly disrupt DSV3's game plan (destroying Pernicious Deed, Sylvan Library, or key lands), so there's a reasonable argument for taking it.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Beast Within from Qwen3L Dreamer's hand
annotations.betterLine: Discard Rishkar's Expertise, which is the highest raw card advantage spell in the hand and could generate a massive swing if it resolves with even a moderate-power creature on board. Without it, Qwen3L Dreamer's hand is mostly fair-rate creatures and a removal spell.

annotations.description: Put Darkblast on top of library instead of Overgrown Tomb, meaning they'll draw Darkblast and potentially miss their 4th land drop. With Pernicious Deed (1BG) and Mystical Teachings (3U) in hand, hitting the 4th land is important for casting these key spells on curve. Darkblast is narrow and doesn't address any immediate threat.

annotations.betterLine: Put Overgrown Tomb on top to ensure the 4th land drop, enabling Pernicious Deed or Mystical Teachings on the following turn. Darkblast can be found later with Sensei's Divining Top or Sylvan Library.

annotations.description: Rishkar's ETB allows putting +1/+1 counters on up to two target creatures. The player only selected Rishkar itself, missing the opportunity to place a second counter on another creature. While there are no other creatures the player controls, the available targets include opponents' creatures. More importantly, placing the counter only on Rishkar (making it 3/3) is fine but the player could have also targeted an opponent's creature like Hada Spy Patrol to give it a counter - though this would actually help the opponent since Rishkar's ability gives creatures with counters '{T}: Add {G}' only for creatures *you* control. So putting a counter on an opponent's creature would just buff it with no mana benefit. However, looking at the board state, Qwen3L Dreamer has Blackblade Reforged on the battlefield but no other creatures besides the entering Rishkar. Putting both counters on Rishkar would make it 4/4 instead of 3/3, which is strictly better since there are no other friendly creatures to target.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected only Rishkar, Peema Renegade for one +1/+1 counter (selected 1 of up to 2 targets, but only 1 own creature available)
annotations.betterLine: This is actually reasonable since the only own creature is Rishkar itself and putting counters on opponents' creatures would only help them. The selection of just Rishkar is correct given the board state.

annotations.description: Qwen3L Dreamer put a +1/+1 counter on an opponent's creature (Hada Spy Patrol, controlled by MiniMx Spike) instead of putting both counters on their own creatures. Rishkar's ability lets you put counters on up to two target creatures — they already targeted their own Rishkar, but the second counter went to an opponent's Hada Spy Patrol. This gives MiniMx Spike a free +1/+1 counter (making the Spy Patrol a 2/2 unblockable creature or advancing its level-up), and also gives it the ability to tap for {G} due to Rishkar's second ability. There's no benefit to buffing an opponent's creature here, especially an evasive one.
annotations.actionTaken: Put the second +1/+1 counter on MiniMx Spike's Hada Spy Patrol
annotations.betterLine: Put both counters on own creatures, or only target Rishkar (selecting only 1 target). Since Rishkar is the only creature Qwen3L controls, they should have selected only Rishkar as the single target rather than giving an opponent a free counter and mana ability.

annotations.description: With Sylvan Library, DSV3 Analyst drew three lands (Island, Overgrown Tomb, Windswept Heath). They need to select 2 to either pay 4 life each or put back on top of library. Selecting Island as one of the two to put back/pay life for is reasonable since it's the weakest card. However, the key question is what the second card should be and whether to pay life. The decision is still in progress (only selected 1 of 2 so far), but choosing Island first is fine. The real consideration is that keeping Windswept Heath (a fetchland) is generally better than keeping a basic Island since it provides deck thinning and can fetch Overgrown Tomb later. Putting Island back on top of the library is the right call for one of the two returns.

annotations.description: Qwen3L Dreamer cast Rishkar's Expertise during the combat phase (the message says 'Play spells and abilities' during COMBAT). Rishkar's Expertise is a sorcery and cannot be cast during combat. However, looking more carefully at the game state, the reasoning mentions 'postcombat main phase' but the decision header says 'Turn 8 COMBAT'. More importantly, the reasoning is completely incoherent - it discusses equipping Blackblade Reforged and Whiptongue Hydra (which isn't on the battlefield), then trails off, yet the actual choice was Rishkar's Expertise. With only 6 mana available (3 Mountains, 2 Forests, 1 Exotic Orchard = 6 lands, but some may be tapped), casting Rishkar's Expertise costs 4GG. The greatest power among their creatures appears to be Kaima at 3/3, so they'd draw 3 cards and get a free spell of MV 5 or less. This is actually a reasonable play if they have the mana. However, they also have Rampant Rejuvenator in hand and an unplayed Mountain. They should play the Mountain first before casting Rishkar's Expertise to have more mana available afterward and to boost Blackblade Reforged's potential. Playing the land before the sorcery is strictly better sequencing.
